newsitem.title: UK: Defector Howarth selected for safe UK Labour seat.
newsitem.headline: Defector Howarth selected for safe UK Labour seat.

text.p: Alan Howarth, the Conservative member of parliament who defected to the opposition Labour Party in 1995, has been selected to fight the safe seat of Newport East at the upcoming general election, a Labour spokesman said.
He said Howarth was chosen from among four aspirants to the candidature at a meeting on Sunday of members of the local constituency party in south Wales.
Labour's Roy Hughes, who is retiring from parliament, won the seat at the 1992 general election with a 9,899 majority.
Howarth is one of four Conservative MPs to have left the party in the last two years.

The two who joined the Liberal Democrats, Emma Nicholson and Peter Thurnham, will not be standing at the election. Sir George Gardiner, who moved to the Referendum Party, will be fighting his Reigate seat in his new party's colours. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
